description: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of sentence counts across eight distinct text categories used in the training data for large language models targeting the Sámi language, as referenced in the paper “Towards a More Inclusive AI: Progress and Perspectives in Large Language Model Training for the Sámi Language.” The vertical axis, labeled “Sentences (K),” represents the number of sentences in thousands, ranging from 0 to over 900K, with tick marks at intervals of 200K. The horizontal axis, labeled “Categories,” lists the following categories in order: Administrative, Religion, Non-fiction, Fiction, Law, News, Science, and an unlabeled gray bar at the far right. Each category is represented by a single vertical bar, with the exact sentence count labeled in blue text above each bar. The “News” category dominates with 902K sentences, followed by “Administrative” at 525K, “Non-fiction” at 190K, “Science” at 110K, “Religion” at 50K, “Fiction” at 35K, and “Law” at 23K. The final gray bar, which lacks a category label, represents only 2K sentences, suggesting it may correspond to a minor or residual category. The bars are not sorted by magnitude, and the chart visually emphasizes the vast disparity in data volume across categories, particularly the overwhelming dominance of News and Administrative texts compared to others like Law and Fiction.
